$comment: Buildings programme Stage 3 / tuning T-1 — THE one tuning file of the reference-library generator (docs/DESIGN_Terrain_Combat_Tuning.md §2a). Every generated number comes from an ammo's driving parameters (ammo.json) and a weapon's (weapons.json) through these coefficients; tuning moves THESE and every type moves together. Deliberately simple engineering approximations — real TKB data always overrides.

kineticPenetration.$comment: pen (mm RHA) = k[type] · v (m/s) · sqrt(mass kg) — a DeMarre-style momentum form; v = the ammo's nominal velocity × the weapon's velocityFactor

shapedChargePenetration.$comment: pen (mm RHA) = coneFactor · calibre (mm), independent of velocity and range; an ammo may state its own coneFactor (an older warhead design)

highExplosivePenetration.$comment: the DIRECT penetration of an HE / fragmentation round on impact (its area effect is CE-1032): pen = factor · calibre

damage.$comment: kinetic: damage = perSqrtJoule · sqrt(½ m v²) (5.56 ball ⇒ ~25, the flat default); explosive types: damage = perKgExplosive · explosive kg

blast.$comment: Hopkinson–Cranz scaled distance: R = Z · W^(1/3), W = explosive kg TNT-equivalent. Inside the lethal radius the blast does lethalDamage; it falls to 0 at the injury radius (CE-1032, docs/DESIGN_Building_Interiors.md §3k W-7′)

fragments.$comment: CE-1032 W-6′ — Gurney fragment velocity v0 = sqrt2E · sqrt(β/(1+β/2)), β = explosive / casing kg (casing = mass − explosive); one fragment's penetration (mm RHA) = kPenetration · v0 · sqrt(m/1000), m = fragmentMassG · max(1, casing / massAnchorCasingKg)^massExponent for HE / frag (⭐ R-2019 D-M1: Mott scaling, 7/9 — a bigger shell throws heavier fragments; the anchor keeps every casing up to the RPG's 0.5 g; a shaped charge keeps fragmentMassG); the reach (m) where fragment damage falls to 0 = radiusPerCbrtCasingKg · casing^(1/3); fragment damage at the burst = damage.perKgExplosive · explosive kg
fragments.$comment2: ⭐ CE-3203 (docs/DESIGN_Building_Interiors.md §3k.1, W-6″) — ONE fragment law for every target: hits = N · area / (2πr² + area), N = casing / m; a fragment's speed falls as e^(−r/λ), λ = dragMetresPerCbrtGram · (m in g)^(1/3); one hit on a MAN does woundPerSqrtJoule · √(½ m v²), on a hull or a weapon perSqrtJoule · √(½ m v²) (a bullet's law). Calibrated so every library round sits near its published lethal / casualty radius (AreaEffectSystemTests.W6pp_*). Absent ⇒ the old dose and reach.
fragments.$comment3: ⭐ CE-3203 — a shaped charge (heat / hedp) fragments only this share of its body: the rest is the rocket motor, the fins and the liner that becomes the jet. 0.02 puts a PG-7V's man at ≈ 126 at 2 m, ≈ 20 at 5 m, ≈ 5 at 10 m.
